title: Apple iPhone Duo review: Two screens, two experiences, two thousand dollars
gist: Ars Technica's review of Apple's $1,999 iPhone Duo foldable finds it technically impressive (near-invisible crease, clever iOS split-screen multitasking, A20 Pro on 2 nm) but compromised as a phone: no Face ID, no telephoto, awkward right-handed ergonomics and a cramped outer screen. The reviewer likens it to early-2010s convertible PCs that were neither great laptops nor great tablets, suggesting a niche rather than mainstream product in its first generation.

insights.speaker: Andrew Cunningham
insights.so_what: Signals the first-gen foldable is a niche product unlikely to drive a broad iPhone upgrade supercycle.
insights.quote: As a little iPad, it’s surprisingly good. As an iPhone, though, I struggle to think of a single way I prefer it to a regular old iPhone.
